subject: human stomach
title: What If You Never Farted Again?

scenes.text: What if you never farted again? The gas would still get out, just not where you think.
Most people pass gas 8 to 14 times a day, between half a liter and a liter and a half.
Hold every bit of it in, and your gut stretches like a balloon: bloating, cramps, even nausea.
Then the trapped gas starts seeping through the wall of your intestines, straight into your blood.
Your blood carries it up to your lungs.
The twist: you'd breathe it out instead. And hold on too long, and it escapes anyway, on its own schedule.

description:
What if you never farted again? Most people pass gas 8 to 14 times a day (NIDDK), roughly 500 to 1,500 mL in total. Holding it in stretches the gut and causes bloating, pain or nausea.
Gas that is not passed is absorbed into the bloodstream and breathed out through the lungs, and if you hold on too long it eventually escapes on its own. About 99% of it is odorless. Not medical advice.
